newsitem.title: USA: Clinton names Berman to lead fast-track effort.
newsitem.headline: Clinton names Berman to lead fast-track effort.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday named Jason Berman, the chairman of the Recording Industry Association of America, to lead the White House effort to win fast-track trade authority from Congress.

"Every president, Republican and Democrat, in the past two decades has had this vital tool to maintain effective American leadership in the global economy," Clinton said in a statement announcing Berman's appointment.

"I am calling on Congress to enact fast-track legislation so we can continue our aggressive drive to open markets to our goods and services and create more high skilled jobs for the American people," he added.

When Congress grants fast-track authority it gives up the right to amend such trade agreements and can only vote for or against them. The administration can therefore negotiate the accords without fear that Congress will seek to change them.

Clinton said Berman will take a leave of absence from his position at the head of the Recording Industry Association of America, a music industry lobbying group, while he is working at the White House as special counselor to the president.
He will be assisted by Victoria Radd, currently a top aide to White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles, in the effort to win fast-track authority.

Seeking to give a push to that effort, Clinton on Thursday was due to meet about two dozen Democratic congressmen to make his case on the matter to members of his own party, White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.
McCurry said the administration is optimistic about the chances of winning the authority.

"There are a lot of concerns that we have to address but given the strength of the economy, and the role that free trade plays in the strength of the economy, we think that we can win the argument at the end of the day," he said.
